# Environment variables

<!-- Generated by apps/web/scripts/env-docs.mjs from apps/web/scripts/env-registry.mjs. Do not edit by hand: change the registry and run `npm run env:docs`. -->

Every variable the site, its scripts and its tools read, found by searching the code (a test fails if the code reads one that is not listed here). Values live in the host's dashboard (Render) and in a local `apps/web/.env` that is never committed. **No value, key, token or password belongs in the repository, a log, a document or a report.**

Check an environment without showing a single value:

```bash
cd apps/web
npm run check:env                      # your local environment (process.env plus apps/web/.env, whose contents are not shown)
npm run check:env -- --env production  # what Render's environment should look like (run it in a shell that has those variables)
```

It reports each variable as present, absent, missing, malformed (wrong prefix, too short, a service key in the publishable slot, a local address in production) or, in production, forbidden or held. In a LOCAL environment it also fails any value that points at the hosted Supabase project: with the three Supabase variables present the site uses real Supabase, so a local file must only ever reach the local stack (`npm run supabase:start`). `CHECK_ENV_ALLOW_HOSTED=1` accepts it deliberately, for one run.

## `apps/web/.env.example`

It must hold **names only**. It is not edited by hand or by the assistants that wrote this repository (access to `.env*` files is blocked for them). Regenerate it from the registry, review the diff, and commit it:

```bash
cd apps/web
node scripts/env-docs.mjs --template > .env.example   # (not `npm run`: npm prints its own banner into the file)
```

## Local development

Nothing is required for the ordinary site: leave `apps/web/.env` with only the mail settings you want to try. To run on the real Supabase stack locally, start it (`npm run supabase:start`) and set these three, to the LOCAL values `npx supabase status` prints (they are not secrets for any real project):

```text
SUPABASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:54321
SUPABASE_ANON_KEY=<the local publishable key>
SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY=<the local secret key>
DATABASE_URL=postgresql://postgres:postgres@127.0.0.1:54322/postgres
```

## Render (production)

Set these in Render's environment, as secrets where the table says so, and nowhere else. The browser never receives any of them: the only variables that reach a page are the `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` ones, none of which is secret (a test checks the code and the built output).

- **Required to run:** `RESEND_API_KEY`, `RESEND_FROM_EMAIL`, `ENQUIRY_EMAIL`, `CAPTCHA_SECRET`, `SUPABASE_URL`, `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`, `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`, `DATABASE_URL`.
- **Stay unset until the owner flips them** (each opens something that is closed by default): `LIBRARY_ENABLED`, `LIBRARY_TERMS_APPROVED`, `ASSISTANT_ENABLED`, `ASSISTANT_PRODUCTION_APPROVED`, `ASSISTANT_MINORS_APPROVED`, `PAPER_TUTOR_ENABLED`, `PAPER_MARKER_ENABLED`, `PAPER_MARKS_RELEASED`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_PORTAL_ENABLED`. In particular `LIBRARY_ENABLED` and `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_PORTAL_ENABLED` are not set as part of the Supabase work.
- **Never set in production** (development, tests or an operator's own shell): `NEXT_PUBLIC_MOTION_DEBUG`, `CAREERS_OPEN_FOR_TESTING`, `DATABASE_ADMIN_URL`, `LEARNTHRIVE_SERVER_PASSWORD`, `SUPABASE_DB_PASSWORD`, `SUPABASE_LOCAL`, `SUPABASE_LOCAL_SERIAL`, `SMOKE_EMAIL`, `CHECK_ENV_ALLOW_HOSTED`, `LIBRARY_DEV_STORAGE_DIR`, `STRIPE_FAKE`, `ASSISTANT_NIM_MODEL`, `ASSISTANT_NIM_VISION_MODEL`, `NVIDIA_API_KEY`, `VOICE_ENABLED`, `VOICE_PROVIDER`, `VOICE_URL`, `VOICE_TOKEN`, `VOICE_HOST`, `VOICE_PORT`, `VOICE_STT_DEVICE`, `VOICE_STT_MODEL`, `VOICE_STT_COMPUTE`, `VOICE_TTS_VOICE`, `LEARNTHRIVE_SUPABASE`, `LEARNTHRIVE_SUPABASE_USE`, `LEARNTHRIVE_DOCKER`, `OLLAMA_MODELS`, `OLLAMA_MODELS_DIR`, `VITE_TURN_URL`, `VITE_TURN_USERNAME`, `VITE_TURN_CREDENTIAL`, `CLOUDFLARE_TURN_KEY_ID`, `CLOUDFLARE_TURN_API_TOKEN`, `TUNNEL_HOST`, `NEXT_DIST_DIR`, `CHROME_PATH`.
- **Secret:** `RESEND_API_KEY`, `CAPTCHA_SECRET`, `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`, `DATABASE_URL`, `DATABASE_ADMIN_URL`, `LEARNTHRIVE_SERVER_PASSWORD`, `SUPABASE_DB_PASSWORD`, `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`, `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, `ASSISTANT_API_KEY`, `NVIDIA_API_KEY`, `VOICE_TOKEN`, `CLOUDFLARE_TURN_KEY_ID`, `CLOUDFLARE_TURN_API_TOKEN`.

## Site and mail

| Variable | What it does | Local | Render production | Secret | Where you get it | If unset |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `NODE_ENV` | Selects production behaviour everywhere (dev-only routes close, fakes are refused). | set by npm run dev | set by next start | no | set by next start / the host | development |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL` | The site's own address: where Stripe sends people back, and an allowed origin. | optional | optional | no | your domain | https://www.learnthrivetuition.co.uk |
| `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` | Comma-separated origins allowed to POST to the site's forms and routes. | optional | optional | no | your domain(s) | the site's own origin (right for production) |
| `RESEND_API_KEY` | Sends the enquiry, careers, account and billing emails. Without it those routes fail closed (503). | optional | required | **yes** | Resend dashboard > API keys | unset |
| `RESEND_FROM_EMAIL` | The verified sender address on your Resend domain. | optional | required | no | Resend dashboard > Domains | onboarding@resend.dev (development only) |
| `ENQUIRY_EMAIL` | Where enquiry notifications go; also the fallback for the other mailboxes. | optional | required | no | your company mailbox | unset |
| `CAREERS_EMAIL` | Where tutor applications (with attachments) and agreement reconfirmations go. | optional | optional | no | your company mailbox | ENQUIRY_EMAIL |
| `SUBJECT_REQUEST_EMAIL` | Where "Can't see your subject?" requests go. | optional | optional | no | your company mailbox | ENQUIRY_EMAIL |
| `LIBRARY_WAITLIST_EMAIL` | Where Library waitlist sign-ups go. | optional | optional | no | your company mailbox | ENQUIRY_EMAIL |
| `CAPTCHA_SECRET` | Signs the site's own human check (no third-party CAPTCHA). Those routes fail closed (503) without it in production. | optional | required | **yes** | generate: node -e "console.log(require('crypto').randomBytes(32).toString('base64url'))" | unset |
| `CLIENT_IP_HEADER` | The request header that carries the visitor's address, if the host sets a trusted one (docs/RENDER.md). | optional | optional | no | your host's documentation, after a test on the deployed service | X-Forwarded-For with TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS |
| `TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS` | How many proxies sit in front of the app, counted from the right of X-Forwarded-For. | optional | optional | no | n/a | 1 |
| `PORT` | The port next start / server.ts listens on. | optional | optional | no | your host sets it | 3000 |
| `CSP_REPORT_ONLY` | 1 sends the Content-Security-Policy as report-only (a staging soak). Build-time. | optional | optional | no | n/a | unset |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_THEME_TOGGLE` | 0 removes the dark theme and the switch (kill switch). Build-time. | optional | optional | no | n/a | on |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_SMOOTH_SCROLL` | 0 removes smooth scrolling (kill switch). Build-time. | optional | optional | no | n/a | on |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_MOTION_DEBUG` | 1 includes the motion debug overlay in a production build. Leave unset. | optional | unset | no | n/a | unset |
| `CAREERS_OPEN_FOR_TESTING` | Opens the careers forms while the safeguarding agreement is a draft. A production build ignores it. | optional | unset | no | n/a | unset |

## Supabase

| Variable | What it does | Local | Render production | Secret | Where you get it | If unset |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `SUPABASE_URL` | The project URL, for Supabase Auth and Storage. With the next two it switches the site to real Supabase, so a local file must point at the LOCAL stack. | required for the real stack (http://127.0.0.1:54321) | required | no | Supabase dashboard > Project Settings > API | unset |
| `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` | The publishable key (sb_publishable_...) or the legacy anon JWT. It grants only what Auth allows anyone. Used by the server only; the browser never calls Supabase. | required for the real stack | required | no | Supabase dashboard > Project Settings > API Keys (publishable) | unset |
| `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` | The secret key (sb_secret_...) or the legacy service_role JWT, for the private storage buckets. It bypasses every policy: server and import tool only. | required for the real stack | required | **yes** | Supabase dashboard > Project Settings > API Keys (secret) | unset |
| `DATABASE_URL` | The server's Postgres connection. Production: the transaction pooler (port 6543), as the narrow learnthrive_server role (scripts/create-server-role.mjs), never postgres. | required for the real stack (postgresql://postgres:postgres@127.0.0.1:54322/postgres) | required | **yes** | Supabase dashboard > Connect (pooler, transaction mode) with the role's password | unset |
| `DATABASE_ADMIN_URL` | The postgres connection used ONLY by scripts/create-server-role.mjs to create the narrow role. An operator's shell session, never a server. | optional | unset | **yes** | the owner, in one shell session | unset |
| `LEARNTHRIVE_SERVER_PASSWORD` | The password to give the learnthrive_server role. Read by create-server-role.mjs from the environment, never written to a file. | optional | unset | **yes** | generate: node -e "console.log(require('crypto').randomBytes(32).toString('base64url'))" | unset |
| `SUPABASE_DB_PASSWORD` | The database password the Supabase CLI asks for on supabase link / db push. One shell session only. | optional | unset | **yes** | the owner (Supabase dashboard > Database settings) | unset |
| `SUPABASE_LOCAL` | 1 enables the tests that need the local Supabase stack (npm run test:realstack sets it). | optional | unset | no | n/a | unset |
| `SUPABASE_LOCAL_SERIAL` | 1, set only by npm run test:realstack: lets the real-stack store test empty the local tables. | optional | unset | no | n/a | unset |
| `SMOKE_EMAIL` | An address you control with NO account yet, for scripts/supabase-smoke.mjs (it signs it up, tests, and deletes it). An existing account is never touched. | optional | unset | no | you: for example a plus-address on your own domain | unset |
| `CHECK_ENV_ALLOW_HOSTED` | 1 lets scripts/check-env.mjs accept hosted Supabase values in a LOCAL environment (it refuses by default so production keys cannot slip into development). | optional | unset | no | n/a | unset |
| `LEARNTHRIVE_SUPABASE` | 0 stops npm run dev from starting the local Supabase stack (the model and voice services are controlled by LEARNTHRIVE_DOCKER). | optional | unset | no | n/a | unset |
| `LEARNTHRIVE_SUPABASE_USE` | 1, set by npm run dev:supabase: the dev server uses the local Supabase stack (real accounts, Library and storage) instead of its in-memory accounts. Development only. | optional | unset | no | n/a | unset |

Off, the work still gets feedback and no mark is shown. | optional | unset until the owner flips it | no | n/a | on in development, off in production |
| `VOICE_ENABLED` | false turns voice off. Ignored in production, where voice is closed. | optional | unset | no | n/a | unset |
| `VOICE_PROVIDER` | sidecar or mock (tests). | optional | unset | no | n/a | sidecar |
| `VOICE_URL` | Where the speech sidecar is. | optional | unset | no | n/a | http://127.0.0.1:8765 |
| `VOICE_TOKEN` | The sidecar's shared secret, if it has one (the same value for the site and the sidecar). | optional | unset | **yes** | generate | unset |
| `VOICE_HOST` | The sidecar's own setting: the address it listens on. | optional | unset | no | n/a | 127.0.0.1 |
| `VOICE_PORT` | The sidecar's own setting: its port. | optional | unset | no | n/a | 8765 |
| `VOICE_STT_DEVICE` | The sidecar's own setting: auto, cpu or cuda. | optional | unset | no | n/a | auto |
| `VOICE_STT_MODEL` | The sidecar's own setting: the Whisper model. | optional | unset | no | n/a | unset |
| `VOICE_STT_COMPUTE` | The sidecar's own setting: float16 or int8. | optional | unset | no | n/a | unset |
| `VOICE_TTS_VOICE` | The sidecar's own setting: the Piper voice. | optional | unset | no | n/a | en_GB-alba-medium |
| `LEARNTHRIVE_DOCKER` | 0 stops npm run dev from starting the model and voice in Docker (the Playwright servers set it). | optional | unset | no | n/a | unset |
| `OLLAMA_MODELS` | Where this machine's Ollama keeps its models; the Docker Ollama mounts the same folder. | optional | unset | no | n/a | unset |
| `OLLAMA_MODELS_DIR` | The same folder, as the compose file names it (defaults to OLLAMA_MODELS). | optional | unset | no | n/a | unset |

## Portal and classroom

| Variable | What it does | Local | Render production | Secret | Where you get it | If unset |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_PORTAL_ENABLED` | true opens the portal (login, dashboards, classroom). Unset is closed in production. Build-time. | optional | unset until the owner flips it | no | n/a | unset |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_CLASSROOM_URL` | Where an external classroom is served; also added to the CSP. | optional | optional | no | n/a | unset |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_TURN_URL` | TURN server URL for classroom video (public by nature). | optional | optional | no | n/a | unset |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_TURN_USERNAME` | TURN username (public by nature: it ships to the browser). | optional | optional | no | n/a | unset |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_TURN_CREDENTIAL` | TURN credential (public by nature: it ships to the browser, so use a short-lived one). | optional | optional | no | n/a | unset |
| `VITE_TURN_URL` | The retired standalone classroom's TURN URL. | optional | unset | no | n/a | unset |
| `VITE_TURN_USERNAME` | The retired standalone classroom's TURN username. | optional | unset | no | n/a | unset |
| `VITE_TURN_CREDENTIAL` | The retired standalone classroom's TURN credential. | optional | unset | no | n/a | unset |
| `CLOUDFLARE_TURN_KEY_ID` | Classroom server (not deployed): with the API token, mints short-lived TURN credentials so the long-lived pair never reaches a browser. | optional | unset | **yes** | Cloudflare dashboard > Realtime > TURN | unset |
| `CLOUDFLARE_TURN_API_TOKEN` | Classroom server (not deployed): the API token of the pair above. Server only. | optional | unset | **yes** | Cloudflare dashboard > Realtime > TURN | unset |
| `TUNNEL_HOST` | Development: a tunnel's host name (for example for testing on a phone), added to the classroom server's allowed origins. | optional | unset | no | n/a | unset |
| `DISCONNECT_GRACE_MS` | Classroom reconnect grace period (apps/realtime and server.ts). | optional | optional | no | n/a | unset |
